_schema.description: Generated by scripts/gap_snapshot.py — do not hand-edit statuses. Lists every gap test that is NOT passing; a test absent from `tests` is expected to pass. CI fails on any divergence in EITHER direction (new failure, or a listed test that now passes). Regenerate with UPDATE_SNAPSHOT=1 ./scripts/run_gap_tests.sh and commit the diff.

fields.issue: GitHub issue tracking this failure, or null when untriaged.
fields.added: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the test first entered the snapshot.
fields.category: ci-env | module-inventory | bug-open | bug-stale | gap-categorical | gap-bisect | untriaged — see test-parity/README.md.

test_gap_prop_plan_cache_invalidation.reason: Root-caused 2026-08-16, no longer 'needs triage'. The test is written for SLOPPY mode (its own comments say "writes must be dropped" / "silent no-op") but runs as ESM, which is strict, so cases 3 and 4 throw instead. Node AND Perry both correctly throw; they differ only in the message. Node names the constructor -- "of object '#<H>'" -- while Perry hardcodes "'#<Object>'" at error.rs:1726, because js_throw_type_error_immutable_write takes (kind, key_ptr, key_len) and no receiver. normalize_failure_output keeps the full error line, so the messages diverge. Real Perry parity bug, not a snapshot artifact: 14 callers, all behind the throw_immutable_write wrapper, so a receiver-aware variant fixes it without a codegen ABI change.
